title_en: China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited, Xi'an Branch v. Shanmei International Energy Group Jincheng Co., Ltd. et al. — contract dispute
ruling_gist_en: A confirmed warehouse receipt transaction is premised on a genuine sales relationship between the parties. If there is no genuine sales relationship, the transaction is deemed a confirmed warehouse receipt transaction in name only but is in substance a loan contract. The confirmed warehouse receipt transaction is invalid, while the concealed loan contract represents the true intention of the parties. If there are no other grounds for invalidity, the loan contract shall be recognized as valid. Where a confirmed warehouse receipt transaction is determined to be a loan contract relationship, this does not affect the validity of the guarantee relationship between the seller and the bank, and the seller shall still bear the guarantee liability.

full_text_en:
China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited, Xi'an Branch v. Shanmei International Energy Group Jincheng Co., Ltd., et al. — Dispute over Contract

【Ruling Summary】

A confirmed warehouse transaction is premised on the existence of a genuine purchase and sale relationship between the parties. Where no genuine purchase and sale relationship exists, the transaction is deemed a loan contract in the guise of a confirmed warehouse transaction. In such circumstances, the confirmed warehouse transaction is invalid, while the concealed loan contract represents the true intention of the parties. If there are no other invalidating circumstances, the loan contract shall be found valid. Where the confirmed warehouse transaction is characterized as a loan contract, the validity of the security relationship between the seller and the bank is not affected, and the seller shall still assume the security liability.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2019) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 870

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Shanmei International Energy Group Jincheng Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 2818, Fengtai West Street, Urban Area, Jincheng City, Shanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Hao Rui, Executive Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Liang Bing, Attorney at Law, Shanghai AllBright Law Offices (Taiyuan).

Agent ad litem: Wang Bei, Attorney at Law, Shanghai AllBright Law Offices (Taiyuan).

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited, Xi'an Branch. Domicile: No. 1, Middle Section of Zhuque Road, Beilin District, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Representative: Hu Bao'an, President of the Branch.

Agent ad litem: Xu Fuqiang, Attorney at Law, Shaanxi Renhe Wanguo Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Liming, Attorney at Law, Shaanxi Renhe Wanguo Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Shaanxi Petrochemical Industry Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 44, Middle Section of Yanta Road, Yanta District, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Guo Xiaohong, Chairman of the Company.

The appellant, Shanmei International Energy Group Jincheng Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanmei Jincheng Company), filed an appeal with this Court against the civil judgment (2017) Shaanxi Civil First Instance No. 11 rendered by the Shaanxi High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance) in the case concerning a contract dispute with the appellees, China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited, Xi'an Branch (hereinafter referred to as CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch) and Shaanxi Petrochemical Industry Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shaanxi Petrochemical Company). After this Court accepted the case and formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, a public hearing was held. Liang Bing and Wang Bei, agents ad litem for Shanmei Jincheng Company, and Xu Fuqiang, agent ad litem for CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch, appeared before the court to participate in the proceedings. Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, having been served with the summons by public announcement, failed to appear before the court. This Court conducted the trial by default in accordance with the law. The case is now concluded.

Shanmei Jincheng Company's grounds of appeal are as follows: 1. The judgment of the court of first instance ordering Shanmei Jincheng Company to refund RMB 162,732,800 to CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch and compensate for interest losses should be set aside in accordance with the law, and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch's claims against Shanmei Jincheng Company should be dismissed. 2. All litigation costs of this case shall be borne by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company. Facts and reasons: (1) The judgment of the court of first instance finding that Shanmei Jincheng Company should bear the liability for the difference refund under the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement was erroneous. The Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement does not constitute a genuine confirmed warehouse transaction and should be invalid, and Shanmei Jincheng Company should not bear any liability. On its face, the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement in question has the characteristics of a confirmed warehouse transaction, but it is not a genuine confirmed warehouse transaction. Rather, it is an arrangement in which CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company colluded to use Shanmei Jincheng Company as the authorized collection party to actually and irregularly provide direct financing to Shaanxi Petrochemical Company. The Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement is void due to the false declaration of intention by the parties; accordingly, Shanmei Jincheng Company cannot be held liable thereunder. The legal consequences of the lending conduct between CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company should be borne by those two parties and are irrelevant to Shanmei Jincheng Company. (2) The finding of the court of first instance that CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch did not neglect to exercise its contractual rights was erroneous, and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch should bear liability in accordance with the law and the agreement. Pursuant to the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement and the corresponding Coal Purchase and Sale Contract, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch provided two rounds of financing to Shaanxi Petrochemical Company. CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch concealed the default by Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and the related evidence during the first round of financing. The court of first instance incorrectly separated the connection between the two rounds of financing and independently assessed CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch's acceptance of the electronic bank acceptance drafts in the second round of financing, thus erroneously concluding that CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch did not neglect to exercise its rights. CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch should bear liability for its own fault. The financing provided by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch to Shaanxi Petrochemical Company exceeded the comprehensive credit line; the loss attributable to the excess amount should be borne by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch. The outstanding debt arising from the second round of financing provided by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch to Shaanxi Petrochemical Company is not a payment for goods under the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement or the Coal Purchase and Sale Contract, and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch cannot demand that Shanmei Jincheng Company bear the liability for the difference refund under the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement. (3) The judgment of the court of first instance erred in its characterization and determination of the nature and effect of the liability for the difference refund. The Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement in question provides for two types of liability: the liability for the difference refund and the liability for the difference guarantee. The only difference between them is the scope of liability. The provision on the liability for the difference refund still serves a security function and is a new type of atypical guarantee. CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch, as a banking financial institution, should have known that the legal representative of Shanmei Jincheng Company, which is a wholly-owned subsidiary of a listed company, had no authority to enter into contracts or agreements containing security content. CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch is not a bona fide third party, and the liability for the difference refund, which has a security nature under the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement entered into between CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch and Shanmei Jincheng Company, is invalid as against Shanmei Jincheng Company. Therefore, Shanmei Jincheng Company should not bear the liability for the difference refund. (4) The judgment of the court of first instance erroneously found that Shanmei Jincheng Company and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company bear joint repayment liability. Even if it is determined that Shanmei Jincheng Company is liable for the difference refund, the liability for the difference refund and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's repayment liability are not the same or joint legal acts, and the bases for claiming these two types of liability are different. It is also unclear whether Shanmei Jincheng Company has a right of recourse after bearing the liability. (5) The basis for the court of first instance's determination that Shanmei Jincheng Company bears liability for interest losses is erroneous. Pursuant to the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement in question, the liability for the difference refund covers only the principal amount of the difference, not interest, liquidated damages, etc. Shanmei Jincheng Company and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch did not reach a consensus on the standard and method for calculating liability for breach of contract. The loss suffered by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch should be proved by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch through evidence. The court of first instance's determination that the liability for breach of contract under the Electronic Bank Acceptance Draft Acceptance Agreement entered into between Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch constitutes the interest loss of CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of Shanmei Jincheng Company.

CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch argued in its defense as follows: (1) The court of first instance correctly categorized the cause of action in this case as a contract dispute. The Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement in question lacks the necessary clauses for a confirmed warehouse transaction, such as warehouse receipt pledge and seller repurchase, and therefore does not constitute a confirmed warehouse agreement. The Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement in question is a financing agreement freely and voluntarily negotiated by the three parties on an equal footing, is lawful and valid, and is binding on all three parties. Article 8 of the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement in question provides that any party that fails to perform or fully perform its agreed obligations shall bear corresponding liability for breach of contract and compensate the other complying parties for all losses caused thereby, including but not limited to principal, interest, penalty interest, etc. Shanmei Jincheng Company and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company acted in malicious collusion and committed a malicious breach of contract. They secretly colluded to discount the electronic bank acceptance drafts that should have been properly held by Shanmei Jincheng Company, thereby damaging the rights and interests of CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch. Accordingly, Shanmei Jincheng Company and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company should bear liability for breach of contract in accordance with the above provision. As for Shanmei Jincheng Company's assertion that CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch colluded with Shaanxi Petrochemical Company to use Shanmei Jincheng Company as the authorized collection party to actually and irregularly provide direct financing to Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, such assertion must be supported by facts and evidence. During the performance of the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement in question, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch was unaware of the breach of contract involving malicious collusion by Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and Shanmei Jincheng Company. It was not until Shanmei Jincheng Company submitted evidence of the private discounting by the two parties during the trial at first instance that CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch discovered the malicious breach of contract by the two parties. It was precisely because CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch relied on the fact that Shanmei Jincheng Company was a subsidiary of a listed company that it entrusted the electronic bank acceptance drafts in question to Shanmei Jincheng Company for safekeeping. However, Shanmei Jincheng Company and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company acted in malicious collusion and, without authorization, discounted the bank drafts in question, creating risks for the transaction. These risks were caused by Shanmei Jincheng Company's own malicious breach of contract, and it should bear liability for such breach. (2) CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch did not neglect to exercise its rights in this case and committed no breach of contract. Each bank acceptance draft issued by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch was strictly in accordance with the provisions of the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement and the Comprehensive Credit Contract. After recovering one draft payment, it issued the next draft on a revolving basis. CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch exercised due diligence during the performance of the contract and did not neglect to exercise its rights. The credit line provided in the Comprehensive Credit Contract in question is RMB 260 million, and this RMB 260 million is the risk exposure amount as defined in Article 1.8 of the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement. The margin deposit paid by Shaanxi Petrochemical Company was RMB 65 million. Adding the risk exposure of RMB 260 million equals RMB 325 million. Therefore, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch did not issue loans in excess of the credit line. The Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement, the Coal Purchase and Sale Contract, and the Electronic Bank Acceptance Draft Acceptance Agreement in question are interrelated and together constitute the complete chain of the financing transaction in this case. Shaanxi Petrochemical Company applied for electronic bank acceptance drafts from CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch in each instance in accordance with the Electronic Bank Acceptance Draft Acceptance Agreement. After receiving the electronic bank acceptance drafts in question, Shanmei Jincheng Company issued a Receipt of Payment Confirmation Notice to CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch in each instance, which is sufficient to prove that the six electronic bank acceptance drafts in question were drafts under the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement. (3) The basis on which CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch demands that Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and Shanmei Jincheng Company bear liability is the provisions on the liability for the difference refund and liability for breach of contract under the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement in question. The breach of contract in this case was jointly committed by Shanmei Jincheng Company and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company through their mutual cooperation. The court of first instance's judgment that Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and Shanmei Jincheng Company bear joint liability is not improper. The liability for the difference refund is a form of non-genuine joint and several liability. If either Shaanxi Petrochemical Company or Shanmei Jincheng Company fulfills its payment obligation, the other's discharge liability is correspondingly reduced. Even if Shanmei Jincheng Company's liability is pursued on the basis of the liability for the difference refund, the court of first instance's judgment ordering joint and several liability is consistent with legal principles and is a practical decision. In conclusion, the appeal by Shanmei Jincheng Company should be dismissed in accordance with the law, and the original judgment should be affirmed.

CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch filed the following claims in the court of first instance: 1. Order Shaanxi Petrochemical Company to repay the principal amount of RMB 162,732,800 of the financing advanced by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch, plus interest of RMB 53,475,600 (calculated on a daily basis at a rate of 0.05% in stages up to November 30, 2016, with interest thereafter calculated in accordance with the contract until the principal is fully paid); 2. Order Shanmei Jincheng Company to refund RMB 162,732,800 to CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch and compensate CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch for interest losses of RMB 53,475,600 (calculated on a daily basis at a rate of 0.05% in stages up to November 30, 2016, with interest thereafter calculated in accordance with the contract until the principal is fully paid); provided that if either Shaanxi Petrochemical Company or Shanmei Jincheng Company fulfills the above payment obligation, the other's discharge liability is correspondingly reduced; 3. Order Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and Shanmei Jincheng Company to jointly bear the litigation costs of this case.

Facts Found by the Court of First Instance: On September 10, 2013, Shanmei Jincheng Company and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company entered into a Coal Sales and Purchase Contract, stipulating that Shanmei Jincheng Company would supply 1.6 million tons of coal to Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, to be executed in two installments over the year; the total contract amount was RMB 704,000,000; the delivery schedule required that no less than 600,000 tons be completed in batches by the end of February 2014, and the cumulative amount of 1.6 million tons be completed by the end of August 2014. The payment method provided that, after the contract was signed, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company would make a prepayment of RMB 352,000,000 in installments within 30 days (by electronic acceptance drafts with terms of seven months, eight months, and ten months, respectively), and any difference would be supplemented or deducted from the next batch of coal payments. On the same day, Shanmei Jincheng Company, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch signed a Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement, stipulating: Whereas Shanmei Jincheng Company and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company have entered or will enter into a purchase and sales contract with coal as the subject matter, and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch have entered or will enter into one or more financing contracts, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch agrees to provide financing to Shaanxi Petrochemical Company in accordance with the financing contracts to pay for Shanmei Jincheng Company's purchase price under the purchase and sales contract. Article 2, Financing Methods, 2.1.1: CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch shall accept bank acceptance drafts for Shaanxi Petrochemical Company with Shanmei Jincheng Company as the payee. 2.2: When applying for financing, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company shall deposit an initial margin as required by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch, which shall be no less than 20% of the proposed financing amount. Article 3, Financing Procedures and Collection Confirmation, 3.3: If the financing method is by electronic bank acceptance draft, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch shall, after the financing is arranged, deliver the Collection Confirmation Notice and the Receipt of Collection Confirmation Notice to the designated contact person of Shanmei Jincheng Company by face-to-face handover or by mail. Upon receipt of the Collection Confirmation Notice, Shanmei Jincheng Company shall immediately verify it against the funds actually received, and after verification, shall sign and seal the Receipt of Collection Confirmation Notice, transmit it to CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch by the designated fax telephone first, and then send the original to CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch by courier within five working days. 3.4: The issuance of the Receipt of Collection Confirmation Notice by Shanmei Jincheng Company to CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch is not a prerequisite for Shanmei Jincheng Company to perform its subsequent obligations (deficiency refund or deficiency guarantee) under this agreement. Article 4, Delivery Mode and Method for Determining Delivery Value, 4.1.1: Item-by-item corresponding mode: After Shaanxi Petrochemical Company reduces the risk exposure of a single financing by repayment, deposit of margin, or other means, it may only apply to take delivery of the goods corresponding to that financing; the deficiency refund/guarantee liability borne by Shanmei Jincheng Company shall also be borne separately based on the difference between the cumulative delivery amount recorded in the Delivery Notice issued by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch under the single financing and the amount collected by Shanmei Jincheng Company. Article 5, Delivery Procedures, 5.1: When Shaanxi Petrochemical Company applies for delivery, it shall submit a Delivery Application stamped with the reserved seal to CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch. If CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch agrees to the delivery, it shall issue a Delivery Notice and send it to Shanmei Jincheng Company by original or fax. The three parties agree that the fax copy shall have the same legal effect as the original. Upon receipt of the original or fax copy, Shanmei Jincheng Company shall verify the relevant seals, signatures, and fax machine numbers, and shall confirm by telephone with the designated contact person of CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch. Only after verification is correct may it arrange delivery for Shaanxi Petrochemical Company. Article 6, Expiration Handling of Delivery Period, 6.1: Thirty days prior to the maturity date of a single financing, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company shall deposit the full margin into the margin account opened by Shaanxi Petrochemical Company at CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch or pay the full financing amount to enable the withdrawal of all goods corresponding to the financing. Otherwise, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company shall be in default, and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch shall have the right to take measures including suspending acceptance of Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's delivery applications, suspending acceptance of Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's financing applications, and declaring part or all of Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's financing at CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch to be immediately due. 6.2: If Shaanxi Petrochemical Company fails to deposit the full margin or pay the full financing amount before the maturity date of the delivery period as provided in Article 6.1, and the cumulative delivery value recorded in the Delivery Notice(s) issued by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch under a single financing or under this agreement is less than the actual amount collected by Shanmei Jincheng Company under that financing or this agreement, Shanmei Jincheng Company shall bear the deficiency refund liability. 6.2.1: After the occurrence of a situation requiring Shanmei Jincheng Company to bear the deficiency refund liability, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch shall serve a Deficiency Refund Payment Notice to Shanmei Jincheng Company by face-to-face handover or by mail. Shanmei Jincheng Company shall, within three working days of receiving the notice, issue a Receipt of the Deficiency Refund Payment Notice to CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch and pay the amount to the account designated by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch in accordance with the notice. Otherwise, without prejudice to any other rights of CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch shall have the right to directly deduct the funds from any account opened by Shanmei Jincheng Company and/or Shaanxi Petrochemical Company (including branches of either party) at any business establishment of CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch. 6.3: Shanmei Jincheng Company guarantees that it shall not refuse the above payment request from CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch on any grounds and waives all rights of defense. 6.5: Shanmei Jincheng Company guarantees that before seeking recourse from Shanmei Jincheng Company, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch need not: 1. First seek recourse from Shaanxi Petrochemical Company; or 2. First take any legal action against Shaanxi Petrochemical Company; or 3. First file a bankruptcy petition against Shaanxi Petrochemical Company. 6.8: CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch is not bound by the purchase contract between Shanmei Jincheng Company and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, and shall not bear any liability or obligation for any disputes or controversies arising between Shanmei Jincheng Company and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company concerning delivery, supply, and the quantity, variety, specification, model, quality, attributes, time limits, after-sales service, etc., of the goods. Any disputes or controversies between Shanmei Jincheng Company and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company shall not affect any rights or interests of CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch under this agreement. Article 7, Declarations and Warranties, 7.1: The three parties are all institutions legally established and lawfully existing, and the signing and performance of this agreement have been effectively approved and fully authorized by their highest authority, and the relevant documents and procedures required for signing this agreement are fully complete and legally valid. 7.2: Shanmei Jincheng Company confirms that any agreement or dispute between Shanmei Jincheng Company and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, or the invalidity of any terms (including any dispute between the parties regarding the Purchase and Sales Contract), shall not affect the deficiency refund/guarantee liability undertaken by Shanmei Jincheng Company under this agreement. Article 8, Liability for Breach of Contract: After this agreement takes effect, Shanmei Jincheng Company, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch shall all honestly perform their obligations under this agreement. Any party that fails to perform or fully perform its obligations under this agreement shall bear corresponding liability for breach of contract and compensate the other complying party(ies) for all losses arising therefrom (including but not limited to principal, interest, penalty interest, compound interest, liquidated damages, damages, and litigation fees, attorney fees, travel expenses, etc. incurred to realize the creditor's rights). On September 12, 2013, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch entered into a Comprehensive Credit Facility Contract, stipulating: Shaanxi Petrochemical Company may apply to CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch for a comprehensive credit facility of RMB 260,000,000 within the usage period of the comprehensive credit facility under this contract; the comprehensive credit facility under this contract may be used for one or more of the following business types: loans, bill acceptance, bill discounting, opening letters of credit, packing loans, import bills, export bills, opening guarantees, or other credit business types recognized by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch; the usage period for the comprehensive credit facility under this contract is one year, from September 12, 2013, to September 12, 2014. The contract also provided that within the usage period and comprehensive credit facility, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company may apply to CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch in writing for use of the comprehensive credit facility in one or multiple installments, and it may be used on a revolving basis. Thereafter, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch entered into an Electronic Bank Acceptance Draft Acceptance Agreement, stipulating that if the bank is not repaid at maturity, penalty interest shall be charged at a daily rate of 0.05% based on the overdue days and overdue payment amount. On September 12, 2013, upon Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's application, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued five electronic bank acceptance drafts with a payee of Shanmei Jincheng Company, with a draft term of seven months, totaling RMB 100,000,000. After Shaanxi Petrochemical Company repaid the corresponding financing amount, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued a delivery notice for RMB 100,000,000 to Shanmei Jincheng Company, and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company took delivery of RMB 100,000,000 worth of goods in March 2014. On September 16, 2013, upon Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's application, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued five electronic bank acceptance drafts with a payee of Shanmei Jincheng Company, with a draft term of eight months, totaling RMB 100,000,000. After Shaanxi Petrochemical Company repaid the corresponding financing amount, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued a delivery notice for RMB 100,000,000 to Shanmei Jincheng Company, and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company took delivery of RMB 100,000,000 worth of goods in April 2014. On September 23, 2013, upon Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's application, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued six electronic bank acceptance drafts with a payee of Shanmei Jincheng Company, with a draft term of ten months, totaling RMB 125,000,000. After Shaanxi Petrochemical Company repaid the corresponding financing amount, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued a delivery notice for RMB 125,000,000 to Shanmei Jincheng Company, and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company took delivery of RMB 125,000,000 worth of goods in July 2014. The above three coal transactions were completed. On April 28, 2014, upon Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's application, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued two electronic bank acceptance drafts with a payee of Shanmei Jincheng Company, with a draft term of ten months, totaling RMB 100,000,000. On May 19, 2014, upon Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's application, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued two electronic bank acceptance drafts with a payee of Shanmei Jincheng Company, with a draft term of ten months, totaling RMB 100,000,000. On August 8, 2014, upon Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's application, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued two electronic bank acceptance drafts with a payee of Shanmei Jincheng Company, with a draft term of seven months, totaling RMB 125,000,000. The above three batches totaled six electronic bank acceptance drafts with a total amount of RMB 325,000,000. After the first batch of drafts matured, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company only repaid the maturing draft amount of RMB 8,350,000, and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch deducted the margin of RMB 65,430,000. Subsequently, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company made further repayments on March 17, 2015, of RMB 10,000,000; on March 27, 2015, of RMB 5,000,000; on April 16, 2015, of RMB 10,000,000; and on April 30, 2015, of RMB 1,220,000. At this point, the principal of the first batch of electronic bank acceptance drafts was fully repaid. After the second batch of electronic bank acceptance drafts matured, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company did not repay any draft amount. After the third batch of electronic bank acceptance drafts matured, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company made repayments on April 30, 2015, of RMB 18,790,000; on May 14, 2015, of RMB 26,477,200; on June 30, 2015, of RMB 8,000,000; and on July 1, 2015, of RMB 9,000,000, totaling principal repayment of RMB 62,267,200 for the third batch. As of the time CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch filed the lawsuit, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company still owed draft principal of RMB 162,732,800 and interest of RMB 53,475,600 (calculated at 0.05% per day, calculated in stages up to November 30, 2016).

Separately, in the Receipt of Collection Confirmation Notices issued by Shanmei Jincheng Company to CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch, the receipts for the three batches of acceptance drafts on September 12, 2013, September 16, 2013, and September 23, 2013, were stamped with the company's "Financial Seal," the receipt for the acceptance draft on April 28, 2014, was stamped with the company's official seal, and the receipts for the acceptance drafts on May 19, 2014, and August 8, 2014, were stamped with the company's "Settlement Center" seal. Additionally, according to evidence provided by Shanmei Jincheng Company, after receiving the RMB 100,000,000 electronic bank acceptance draft issued by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch on May 19, 2014, Shanmei Jincheng Company, upon the instruction of Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, paid the entire RMB 100,000,000 to Ma'anshan Aoxing Metal Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Ma'anshan Aoxing Company). On August 8, 2014, after receiving the RMB 125,000,000 electronic bank acceptance draft, Shanmei Jincheng Company, upon the instruction of Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, paid RMB 121,084,571.87, the amount after discounting the acceptance draft, to Shenzhen Datang Industry and Trade Co., Ltd.

The Court of First Instance held that the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement signed on September 10, 2013, by Shanmei Jincheng Company, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch represented the true intentions of all parties, did not violate the prohibitive provisions of laws and regulations, and should be a valid contract. The agreement provided that Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch had entered or would enter into one or more financing contracts, and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch agreed to provide financing to Shaanxi Petrochemical Company in accordance with the financing contracts to pay for Shanmei Jincheng Company's purchase price under the purchase and sales contract. On September 12, 2013, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch entered into a Comprehensive Credit Facility Contract. Subsequently, on September 12, 2013, September 16, 2013, and September 23, 2013, upon Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's application, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued electronic bank acceptance drafts with Shanmei Jincheng Company as payee, totaling RMB 325,000,000, and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company took delivery of goods of the corresponding value in installments, which was not disputed by any party. On April 28, 2014, May 19, 2014, and August 8, 2014, upon Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's application, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch additionally issued six electronic bank acceptance drafts with Shanmei Jincheng Company as payee, totaling RMB 325,000,000. After repaying part of the draft amounts, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company still owed CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch draft principal of RMB 162,732,800 and interest of RMB 53,475,600. In summary, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch performed its obligation to issue electronic bank acceptance drafts for Shaanxi Petrochemical Company in accordance with the agreement. Shaanxi Petrochemical Company failed to repay the draft amounts and should bear corresponding liability for breach of contract. Shanmei Jincheng Company should also bear the deficiency refund and corresponding liability for breach of contract in accordance with the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement.

The disputed issues in this case at first instance were: 1. Whether the six electronic bank acceptance drafts in question were financing under the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement; 2. Whether CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch was negligent in exercising its rights; 3. The nature and validity of the deficiency refund liability of Shanmei Jincheng Company under the contract; 4. The basis for calculating interest losses.

1. Regarding the three batches of six electronic bank acceptance drafts totaling RMB 325,000,000 on April 28, 2014, May 19, 2014, and August 8, 2014, Shanmei Jincheng Company argued that it had never confirmed them, so they were not financing under the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement, and it should not bear the deficiency refund liability. Upon examination, Shanmei Jincheng Company did not dispute having received the above six electronic bank acceptance drafts. For the two electronic bank acceptance drafts on April 28, 2014, Shanmei Jincheng Company acknowledged having issued the Receipt of Collection Confirmation Notice and assumed corresponding responsibility. For the two batches of four electronic bank acceptance drafts on May 19, 2014, and August 8, 2014, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch submitted the Receipts of Collection Confirmation Notices issued by Shanmei Jincheng Company after receiving the four electronic bank acceptance drafts. Shanmei Jincheng Company objected to the "Settlement Center" seal affixed thereon and applied for authentication. The Court of First Instance held that, apart from the company's official seal, Shanmei Jincheng Company had also used seals such as the "Financial Seal" on multiple receipts, indicating that there was no fixed requirement or practice between the parties regarding the affixing of seals. Therefore, its argument that the affixing of the "Settlement Center" seal did not conform to the settlement practices of the parties could not be sustained. Furthermore, according to Article 3.4 of the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement, the issuance of the Receipt of Collection Confirmation Notice by Shanmei Jincheng Company to CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch is not a prerequisite for Shanmei Jincheng Company to perform its subsequent obligations under this agreement. Therefore, whether Shanmei Jincheng Company issued a receipt to CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch does not affect CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch's right to claim against it under the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement. Moreover, Shanmei Jincheng Company had no evidence to deny the authenticity of the "Settlement Center" seal, so its application for authentication of the seal on the receipts was not granted. Shanmei Jincheng Company also argued that, under the circumstances where the Coal Sales and Purchase Contract had unclear terms and no consensus was reached with Shaanxi Petrochemical Company on how to perform the second batch of goods, the three batches of financing totaling RMB 325,000,000 provided by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch to Shaanxi Petrochemical Company were not amounts under the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement. Upon examination, Article 6.8 of the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement stipulates that CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch is not bound by the purchase contract between Shanmei Jincheng Company and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company. The Court of First Instance held that after CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued and delivered the electronic bank acceptance drafts, the nature of its actions was not affected by subsequent actions of others. How Shanmei Jincheng Company exercised its rights after obtaining the negotiable instrument rights, whether it benefited from the drafts, whether Shaanxi Petrochemical Company applied for delivery, and whether the subsequent transaction process was completed were not matters that CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch could determine and did not affect the nature of CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch's issuance of acceptance drafts as performance of the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement. Although Shanmei Jincheng Company did not recognize the six electronic bank acceptance drafts in question as amounts under the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement, it could not provide evidence to prove that it had other legitimate grounds for receiving those electronic bank acceptance drafts. In summary, Shanmei Jincheng Company's claim that the six electronic bank acceptance drafts in question were not financing under the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement lacked factual basis and was not adopted according to law.

2. Regarding Shanmei Jincheng Company's claim that CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch was negligent in exercising its rights. Upon examination, in the first round of three batches of financing provided by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch to Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company repaid the financing amounts before the maturity of the acceptance drafts and took delivery of the corresponding goods. In the second round of financing, after CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued the first batch of electronic bank acceptance drafts on April 28, 2014, it subsequently issued the second and third batches of electronic bank acceptance drafts on May 19, 2014, and August 8, 2014, upon Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's application. At the time of issuing the second and third batches of electronic bank acceptance drafts, the first batch had not yet matured. Shanmei Jincheng Company's argument that the latter two batches of financing were extended while Shaanxi Petrochemical Company was in continuous default from March to July 2014 was inconsistent with the facts. Therefore, its argument that CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch was negligent in exercising its rights, causing expanded losses, and that it should not be required to bear those losses, could not be sustained and was not supported according to law.

3.  Regarding the nature and validity of Shanmei Jincheng Company's liability for the shortfall refund under the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement.

Shanmei Jincheng Company argued that the essence of the shortfall refund liability was the provision of a guarantee, and because the company's legal representative had no authority to sign a guarantee agreement externally, the clause was invalid. The court of first instance held that the shortfall refund liability was not a guarantee. First, Article 6.2 of the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement provided for both shortfall refund and shortfall guarantee, which were clearly two different forms of liability, and the parties in this case chose the shortfall refund liability method. Second, Shanmei Jincheng Company's shortfall refund liability was based on liability for breach of contract arising from its violation of the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement, which differed from the guarantor's liability as a secondary obligation based on a guarantee contract. Third, as the payee of the bank acceptance drafts involved in this case, Shanmei Jincheng Company could have fully controlled its own risk if it had strictly performed its obligations under the contract; however, during actual performance, Shanmei Jincheng Company violated the contract by paying the bank acceptance drafts to a third party at the request of Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, resulting in the inability to recover the draft proceeds, for which Shanmei Jincheng Company was at fault. In summary, Shanmei Jincheng Company's argument that the nature of the shortfall refund liability was a guarantee could not be established, and its claim that the clause was invalid on this basis was not supported by law and was denied.

4.  Regarding the basis for calculating interest losses.

The Electronic Bank Acceptance Draft Acceptance Agreement entered into between Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch stipulated that for draft proceeds not paid by the bank on the maturity date, penalty interest would be charged at a daily interest rate of 0.05% based on the number of overdue days and the overdue payment amount. CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch's claim for interest losses from Shaanxi Petrochemical Company at a daily rate of 0.05% had a contractual basis. The Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement entered into between Shanmei Jincheng Company, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, and CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch stipulated that any party that failed to perform or fully perform its obligations under this agreement shall bear corresponding liability for breach of contract and compensate the other observing parties for all losses caused thereby (including but not limited to principal, interest, penalty interest, compound interest, liquidated damages, damages for loss, and litigation fees, attorney fees, travel expenses, etc. incurred for realizing the creditor's rights). Because Shanmei Jincheng Company failed to perform the shortfall refund liability as stipulated in the contract, it constituted a breach of contract, and it should bear corresponding liability for breach of contract and compensate CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch for all losses caused thereby, which losses should include the interest losses calculated at the above-mentioned daily rate of 0.05%. Therefore, CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch's claim for interest losses had a contractual basis and was supported by law.

In summary, for the principal and interest of the unpaid draft proceeds in this case, both Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and Shanmei Jincheng Company were obligated to fully repay and should bear joint repayment liability. Pursuant to Article 60 and Article 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and Shanmei Jincheng Company shall, within thirty days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective, pay CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch the principal of the draft proceeds in the amount of RMB 162,732,800 and the interest (interest of RMB 53,475,600 as of November 30, 2016, and interest calculated at a daily rate of 0.05% from December 1, 2016, until the date of actual payment). If the monetary payment obligation is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The court acceptance fee of RMB 1,122,842 and the preservation fee of RMB 5,000 (prepaid by CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch) shall be borne by Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and Shanmei Jincheng Company.

This court holds that, based on the appeal and defense opinions of the parties, the focus of the dispute in this second instance is: Whether the court of first instance correctly ordered Shanmei Jincheng Company to pay the principal of the draft proceeds of RMB 162,732,800 and interest to CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch.

I. Regarding the validity of the Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement involved in the case.

Confirmed warehouse receipt financing, as a new type of financing and security arrangement, has a basic transaction model that uses bank credit as a carrier, bank acceptance drafts as settlement instruments, bank control of the title to the goods, the seller as the custodian of the goods, and the difference between the acceptance draft and the margin as security. The basic transaction process of confirmed warehouse receipt financing is as follows: the seller, the buyer, and the bank sign a tripartite cooperation agreement, under which the buyer deposits a certain percentage of the acceptance margin with the bank; the bank issues a bank acceptance draft to the buyer with the seller as the payee; the buyer delivers the bank acceptance draft to the seller as payment for the goods; the bank issues a delivery order to the seller based on a certain percentage of the margin paid by the buyer; the seller delivers goods of the corresponding amount to the buyer according to the delivery order; after selling the goods, the buyer deposits the proceeds as margin. According to the contents of the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement" involved in this case, the transaction method agreed upon by the parties in that agreement is a relatively typical confirmed warehouse receipt financing transaction. However, confirmed warehouse receipt financing is premised on the existence of a genuine sales relationship between the buyer and seller. Although the transaction method reflected in the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement" involved in this case is confirmed warehouse receipt financing, according to the facts found, there was no genuine goods sales transaction between Shanmei Jincheng Company and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company. The confirmed warehouse receipt financing involved in the case lacked a genuine trade background; therefore, no genuine and valid legal relationship of confirmed warehouse receipt financing existed among the parties. The genuine legal relationship among the parties to the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement" involved in the case should be that of a loan and guarantee contract, i.e., China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch provided financing loans to Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, and Shanmei Jincheng Company provided a guarantee for Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's loan to China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch. The above loan and guarantee were the genuine expression of the parties' intent and did not violate legal provisions; therefore, the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement" involved in the case is essentially a loan and guarantee contract and should be deemed valid.

Article 1.6 of the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement" involved in the case stipulates that deficiency refund means that if Shaanxi Petrochemical Company fails to deposit sufficient margin or fully repay the financing to China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch within the agreed time, and the cumulative value of goods taken under the "Delivery Order" issued by China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch under this agreement is less than the amount received by Shanmei Jincheng Company, then Shanmei Jincheng Company shall refund the deficiency as required by China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch. Article 1.7 stipulates that deficiency guarantee means that if Shaanxi Petrochemical Company fails to deposit sufficient margin or fully repay the financing to China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch within the agreed time, and the cumulative value of goods taken under the "Delivery Order" issued by China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch under this agreement is less than the amount received by Shanmei Jincheng Company, then Shanmei Jincheng Company shall refund the deficiency within the time required by China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch, and shall assume joint and several guarantee liability for the amount to be refunded and the financing interest of Shaanxi Petrochemical Company arising from the failure to timely refund, overdue interest and penalty interest arising from the overdue financing of Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, and other related expenses. Article 6.2 stipulates that if Shaanxi Petrochemical Company fails to deposit the full margin or pay off the full financing before the expiry of the delivery period as agreed in Article 6.1, and the cumulative value of goods taken under the "Delivery Order" issued by China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch under a single financing or this agreement is less than the actual amount received by Shanmei Jincheng Company for that financing or under this agreement, Shanmei Jincheng Company bears the deficiency refund liability. According to the above stipulations, although the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement" involved in the case specifies two forms of liability, namely deficiency refund and deficiency guarantee, and the parties to this case agreed on the form of deficiency refund liability, in essence, whether deficiency refund or deficiency guarantee, both are that Shanmei Jincheng Company assumes guarantee liability to China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch for the deficiency of the financing amount when Shaanxi Petrochemical Company fails to repay the financing to China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch. Article 18 of the Guarantee Law of the PRC stipulates: "If the parties agree in the guarantee contract that the guarantor and the debtor are jointly and severally liable for the debt, it is a joint and several liability guarantee. If the debtor of a joint and several liability guarantee fails to perform the debt upon the expiration of the debt performance period stipulated in the main contract, the creditor may demand the debtor to perform the debt, or may demand the guarantor to assume guarantee liability within its guarantee scope." Article 19 stipulates: "If the parties have not agreed on the method of guarantee or the agreement is unclear, the guarantor shall assume guarantee liability in accordance with joint and several liability guarantee." Article 6.5 of the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement" involved in the case stipulates that Shanmei Jincheng Company guarantees that before China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch claims against Shanmei Jincheng Company, it is not necessary: 1. to first claim against Shaanxi Petrochemical Company; or 2. to first take any legal action against Shaanxi Petrochemical Company; or 3. to first file a bankruptcy petition against Shaanxi Petrochemical Company. According to the above legal provisions and the agreement, Shanmei Jincheng Company should bear joint and several guarantee liability. The first instance judgment's determination that the deficiency refund liability agreed upon in the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement" involved in the case was not a guarantee was somewhat improper. The "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement" involved in the case was stamped with the official seal of Shanmei Jincheng Company and signed by its legal representative. Article 7.1 of the agreement clearly stipulates that "the three parties are all institutions established and legally existing, and the signing and performance of this agreement have been effectively approved and fully authorized by their highest authority, and the relevant documents and procedures required for signing this agreement are fully complete, lawful, and effective." Therefore, the appeal ground of Shanmei Jincheng Company that its legal representative had no right to sign a contract or agreement with guarantee nature, and that the deficiency refund liability with guarantee nature in the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement" was invalid against Shanmei Jincheng Company, cannot be established.

2. Regarding whether the six electronic bank acceptance drafts involved in the case were issued for the performance of the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement"

Shanmei Jincheng Company, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, and China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch signed the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement" involved in the case on September 10, 2013, with a validity period of two years. The six electronic bank acceptance drafts involved in the case were issued within the validity period stipulated in the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement". Shanmei Jincheng Company did not dispute the fact of receiving the six electronic bank acceptance drafts involved in the case. China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch submitted the "Receipt of Confirmation Notice of Receipt". Shanmei Jincheng Company also could not provide evidence to prove that it had other legal grounds for receiving the drafts. The first instance court had sufficient basis for not accepting Shanmei Jincheng Company's claim that the six electronic bank acceptance drafts involved in the case were not financing under the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement". The appeal ground of Shanmei Jincheng Company that the overdue amounts under the six electronic bank acceptance drafts involved in the case were not the payment for goods under the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement" and the "Coal Sales Contract", and that China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch could not claim deficiency refund liability against Shanmei Jincheng Company based on the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement", lacks factual and legal basis and cannot be established.

3. Regarding the issue of Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's liability

Based on the financing loan contract relationship between China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, in accordance with the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement", "Comprehensive Credit Facility Agreement", etc., and upon the application of Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued bank acceptance drafts and made payment on the maturity date of the bank acceptance drafts. Shaanxi Petrochemical Company only repaid part of the amounts. The first instance judgment ordering Shaanxi Petrochemical Company to pay China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch the overdue principal of the draft amount and interest had clear findings of fact and correct application of law. Shaanxi Petrochemical Company did not appeal this. The part of the first instance judgment regarding Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's liability should be upheld. Article 2.1 of the "Comprehensive Credit Facility Agreement" involved in the case stipulates that the comprehensive credit facility available to Shaanxi Petrochemical Company for application to China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch during the usage period of the comprehensive credit facility under this contract is RMB 260,000,000. Article 3.3.1 stipulates that during the usage period of the comprehensive credit facility, for the comprehensive credit facility that has been repaid by Shaanxi Petrochemical Company, China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch agrees to handle it on a revolving basis, i.e., under the comprehensive credit facility stipulated in Article 2 of this contract, if the debt of Shaanxi Petrochemical Company to China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch has been repaid during the usage period of the above comprehensive credit facility, China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch shall restore the corresponding facility to Shaanxi Petrochemical Company for the repaid portion, and Shaanxi Petrochemical Company may reuse it during the usage period of the comprehensive credit facility. According to the above stipulations, the comprehensive credit facility of RMB 260,000,000 could be used on a revolving basis. The six bank acceptance drafts involved in the case were not issued at the same time but were issued in three batches. Moreover, in this case, Shaanxi Petrochemical Company deposited a margin of RMB 65,430,000. There was no fact that China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued loans exceeding the credit facility in this case. The appeal ground of Shanmei Jincheng Company that China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch issued loans exceeding the credit facility and that China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch should bear liability for losses on the excess portion lacks factual and legal basis and cannot be established.

4. Regarding the issue of Shanmei Jincheng Company's liability

As mentioned above, Shanmei Jincheng Company should bear joint and several guarantee liability for Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's loan to China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch. According to Articles 1.6 and 6.2 of the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement", the scope of Shanmei Jincheng Company's guarantee liability is the overdue principal of the draft amount. Article 6.2.1 of the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement" stipulates that when a situation requiring Shanmei Jincheng Company to bear deficiency refund liability occurs, China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch shall deliver the "Notice of Payment for Deficiency Refund" to Shanmei Jincheng Company by handover in person or by mail. Shanmei Jincheng Company shall, within 3 working days after receiving the notice, issue a "Receipt of the Notice of Payment for Deficiency Refund" to China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch and pay the amount to the account designated by China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch as required by the notice. Otherwise, without prejudice to any other rights of China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch, China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch has the right to directly deduct the funds from any account opened by Shanmei Jincheng Company and/or Shaanxi Petrochemical Company (including branches of both parties) in all business institutions of China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch. Article 8 stipulates that any party that fails to perform or fails to fully perform the obligations agreed upon in this agreement shall bear the corresponding liability for breach of contract and compensate the other non-breaching party for all losses incurred (including but not limited to principal, interest, penalty interest, compound interest, liquidated damages, damages for losses, and litigation fees, attorney fees, travel expenses, etc. incurred for realizing the claim). In summary, although according to the agreement on deficiency refund liability in the "Tripartite Business Cooperation Agreement", the scope of Shanmei Jincheng Company's guarantee is the principal of the overdue amount, according to the agreement on liability for breach of contract in the agreement, if Shanmei Jincheng Company fails to pay the amount to the account designated by China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch as required within 3 working days after receiving the "Notice of Payment for Deficiency Refund" delivered by China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch, it constitutes a breach of contract, and it shall bear compensation liability for the interest, penalty interest, compound interest, liquidated damages, damages for losses, and litigation fees, attorney fees, travel expenses, etc. incurred for realizing the claim from the date of its breach. According to the above agreement, Shanmei Jincheng Company should, within 3 working days after receiving the "Notice of Payment for Deficiency Refund", pay the amount to the account designated by China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch as required by the notice. Although China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch submitted a "Notarized Certificate" to prove that it mailed a "Letter on Immediately Fulfilling the Obligation of Deficiency Refund" to Shanmei Jincheng Company on August 19, 2015, Shanmei Jincheng Company denied receiving the letter. China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch did not provide sufficient evidence to prove that Shanmei Jincheng Company actually received the letter and the exact time of receipt. China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch filed this lawsuit, and Shanmei Jincheng Company received the first instance complaint of China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch on November 17, 2017. Therefore, this court determines that Shanmei Jincheng Company bears liability for interest on the overdue amount of Shaanxi Petrochemical Company from November 20, 2017. This court corrects the start date for Shanmei Jincheng Company's interest liability as determined in the first instance judgment. Shanmei Jincheng Company bears joint and several guarantee liability. The first instance judgment ordering Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and Shanmei Jincheng Company to bear joint liability, without clearly distinguishing the nature of the liability borne by Shaanxi Petrochemical Company and Shanmei Jincheng Company, was somewhat improper and should be corrected. This appeal ground of Shanmei Jincheng Company is established, and this court supports it. Shanmei Jincheng Company bears joint and several guarantee liability. According to Article 31 of the Guarantee Law of the PRC, after assuming liability, it may seek recourse from Shaanxi Petrochemical Company.

In summary, regarding the part of the first instance judgment on Shaanxi Petrochemical Company's liability, the facts were clearly found and the law was correctly applied, and it should be upheld. The determination of the nature of Shanmei Jincheng Company's liability and the start date for interest was somewhat improper and should be corrected. In accordance with Items 1 and 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this court hereby renders the following judgment:

1. The Civil Judgment (2017) Shan Civil First Instance No. 11 of the Shaanxi High People's Court is amended as follows: Shaanxi Petrochemical Industry Group Co., Ltd. shall, within thirty days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective, pay to China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch the overdue principal of the draft amount of RMB 162,732,800 and interest (the interest up to November 30, 2016, is RMB 53,475,600, plus interest calculated at a daily rate of 0.05% from December 1, 2016, to the date of actual payment);

2. Shanmei International Energy Group Jincheng Co., Ltd. shall bear joint and several guarantee liability for the overdue principal of the draft amount of RMB 162,732,800 and interest (calculated at a daily rate of 0.05% from November 20, 2017, to the date of actual payment) payable by Shaanxi Petrochemical Industry Group Co., Ltd. to China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch; after assuming guarantee liability, Shanmei International Energy Group Jincheng Co., Ltd. has the right to seek recourse from Shaanxi Petrochemical Industry Group Co., Ltd.;

3. Other appeal claims of Shanmei International Energy Group Jincheng Co., Ltd. are rejected;

4. Other litigation claims of China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch are rejected.

If payment of the monetary obligation is not made within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

The first instance acceptance fee of RMB 1,122,842 shall be borne by Shaanxi Petrochemical Industry Group Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 673,705 and by Shanmei International Energy Group Jincheng Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 449,137; the preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne by Shanmei International Energy Group Jincheng Co., Ltd. The second instance acceptance fee of RMB 1,122,842 shall be borne by Shanmei International Energy Group Jincheng Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 842,132 and by China CITIC Bank Xi'an Branch in the amount of RMB 280,710.

This judgment is final.
